title: Leo, the old lizard.
lines: In a primary school classroom, in a glass tank, lives a lizard.
His name is Leo.
Leo is very old.
He is seventy-four years old!
He has lived in this classroom his whole life.
Every year new children come.
And every year Leo watches them from behind his glass.
A turtle lives in the same tank.
His name is Squirtle.
Squirtle is old too, and a bit grumpy.
He talks all day long.
Leo and Squirtle have been friends for a very long time.
One day Leo hears something that gives him a fright.
A lizard like you only lives to be seventy-five, the teacher tells the children.
Leo counts.
Seventy-four.
Only one more year!
There are so many things I haven't done yet, he thinks.
I've never been outside.
I've never seen the sea.
I have to escape!
Leo makes a plan to escape.
But then a new teacher comes.
She's strict.
She says: Every weekend a child takes the class pet home.
To look after it.
The first weekend Leo goes home with a girl.
Her name is Summer.
Summer talks a lot.
So much that the other children find her a bit annoying.
She always sits alone.
In her room Summer puts Leo's tank on her desk.
She tells him about her day.
And then, wow, Leo talks back.
You can talk!
shouts Summer.
Shhh, says Leo.
It's a secret.
Nobody must know.
But you know what?
I can help you.
Leo says to Summer: Try listening.
Let the other children tell you things too.
Ask questions.
Then they'll want to talk to you.
On Monday Summer tries it.
She listens.
She asks questions.
And do you know what?
Two girls want to sit next to her at lunch.
Summer is so happy.
Every weekend Leo goes to a different child.
A boy who is scared of swimming.
Leo says to him: Everyone is scared of something.
Start small.
First put your feet in the water.
A girl who can't sleep because her mummy and daddy are arguing.
Leo listens to her.
He says: It's not your fault.
And you can tell someone you trust.
A boy who always plays on his tablet and never goes outside.
Leo takes him into the garden.
Look, says Leo.
A real butterfly.
Much more beautiful than on your screen.
Every child thinks Leo only talks to them.
Every child thinks they share a secret with Leo.
But Leo helps them all.
And slowly the children change.
They become braver.
They become kinder.
They help each other.
One day the children find out that Leo talks to everyone.
At first they're a bit cross.
But then they realise something.
Leo helped all of us, says Summer.
Now we have to help him.
Because the children know about Leo's big wish.
He wants to see the world before it's too late.
On the last day of the school year the children go on a trip.
To the seaside!
They take Leo with them, in a little basket.
Leo sees the sea for the first time.
The water is so big and so blue.
The waves whoosh.
The sun shines warmly on his scales.
He feels the sand under his feet.
This is the most beautiful thing I've ever seen, whispers Leo.
And do you know the best news of all?
The teacher checked.
She was wrong.
Lizards like Leo can live much longer than seventy-five.
Even a hundred years!
Leo still has lots and lots of time.
He sighs with relief.
And he smiles.
After the summer new children come to the class.
And Leo is back in his glass tank, with Squirtle.
Ready to listen.
Ready to help.
The end.
